symbols.name: V
symbols.def: \(V\) is the set of observed substantive variables.

symbols.name: S
symbols.def: \(S=1\) denotes membership in the observed subpopulation.

symbols.name: sigma
symbols.space: families of finite state spaces on \(V\cup\{S\}\)
symbols.def: \(\sigma=(\mathcal X_v)_{v\in V\cup\{S\}}\) satisfies \(2\le |\mathcal X_v|<\infty\) for every \(v\in V\) and \(\mathcal X_S=\{0,1\}\).

symbols.name: sigmabin
symbols.def: \(\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}}\) is the signature with \(\mathcal X_v=\{0,1\}\) for every \(v\in V\cup\{S\}\).

symbols.name: G
symbols.type: finite augmented acyclic directed mixed graph
symbols.space: ADMGs on \(V\cup\{S\}\) in which \(S\) has no children
symbols.def: \(G^S\) has an acyclic directed part, \(S\) has no children, and its directed and bidirected edges encode permitted, possibly inactive, structural dependences.

symbols.name: X
symbols.def: \(X\subseteq V\) is the set intervened upon.

symbols.name: Y
symbols.def: \(\varnothing\ne Y\subseteq V\setminus X\) is the queried outcome set.

symbols.name: x
symbols.def: \(x\in\mathcal X_X\) is a fixed value assigned to \(X\) within signature \(\sigma\).

symbols.name: xbin
symbols.def: \(x_{\mathrm{bin}}\in\{0,1\}^{X}\) is an intervention value returned with a binary nonidentification certificate.

symbols.name: AS
symbols.def: \(A_S=V\cap\operatorname{An}_{G^S}(S)\).

symbols.name: NS
symbols.def: \(N_S=V\setminus A_S\).

symbols.name: XS
symbols.def: \(X_S=X\cap A_S\).

symbols.name: XN
symbols.def: \(X_N=X\cap N_S\).

symbols.name: xS
symbols.def: \(x_S=x|_{X_S}\) is the restriction of the intervention value to \(X_S\).

symbols.name: xN
symbols.def: \(x_N=x|_{X_N}\) is the restriction of the intervention value to \(X_N\).

symbols.name: YS
symbols.def: \(Y_S=Y\cap A_S\).

symbols.name: YN
symbols.def: \(Y_N=Y\cap N_S\).

symbols.name: W
symbols.def: \(W=A_S\setminus(X_S\cup Y_S)\).

symbols.name: D
symbols.def: \(D=\operatorname{An}_{G^S[N_S\setminus X_N]}(Y_N)\).

symbols.name: DS
symbols.def: \(\mathcal D_S(D)=\{D_1,\ldots,D_k\}\) is the S-component partition of \(D\) in \(G^S[D\cup A_S\cup\{S\}]\).

symbols.name: H
symbols.def: \(H\subseteq N_S\) is a generic set used in S-component and selected-kernel operations.

symbols.name: C
symbols.def: \(C=D_i\) is the fixed target S-component from \(\mathcal D_S(D)\) in a terminal call descended from Algorithm 1's initial call for \(D_i\).

symbols.name: T
symbols.def: \(T\) is the enclosing single S-component in a terminal failed call descended from \(\operatorname{sID\text{-}Single}(D_i,T_i^{(0)},Q_{P_\sigma}^S[T_i^{(0)}])\), with \(C=D_i\subsetneq T\subseteq T_i^{(0)}\).

symbols.name: M
symbols.type: signature-indexed recursive augmented structural causal model
symbols.space: augmented SCMs on \(V\cup\{S\}\) with endogenous signature \(\sigma\) and mutually independent exogenous variables that may be shared across multiple endogenous mechanisms
symbols.def: \(M\) is a generic recursive augmented SCM with endogenous state spaces \(\sigma\) compatible with \(G^S\); each exogenous variable may enter several endogenous mechanisms, and the resulting directed and pairwise bidirected adjacencies must be permitted by \(G^S\).

symbols.name: Mplus
symbols.space: sets of recursive augmented SCMs with arbitrary shared exogenous incidence
symbols.def: \(\mathfrak M_+(G^S,\sigma)\) is defined in \(\mathrm{def:model\text{-}class}\).

symbols.name: M0
symbols.def: \(M_0\) is the first model in a within-signature observational-equivalence comparison.

symbols.name: M1
symbols.def: \(M_1\) is the second model in a within-signature observational-equivalence comparison.

symbols.name: CertSCM
symbols.space: finite rational table encodings for the binary signature
symbols.def: \(\operatorname{CertSCM}(G^S,\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}})\) is the exact certificate type defined in \(\mathrm{def:certscm\text{-}encoding\); its latent factors may each enter any finite number of endogenous mechanisms.

symbols.name: RealizeCert
symbols.def: \(\llbracket E\rrbracket\) is the augmented SCM obtained by interpreting the finite latent and structural tables in \(E\in\operatorname{CertSCM}(G^S,\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}})\).
symbols.role: bridge from finite encoding to the ambient model class

symbols.name: E0
symbols.def: \(E_0\) is the first finitely encoded rational failure witness, with realized model \(\llbracket E_0\rrbracket\).

symbols.name: E1
symbols.def: \(E_1\) is the second finitely encoded rational failure witness, with realized model \(\llbracket E_1\rrbracket\).

symbols.name: CertCheck
symbols.def: \(\mathsf{Check}_{\mathrm{NONID}}\) is the exhaustive rational-arithmetic checker defined in \(\mathrm{def:certificate\text{-}checker\).

symbols.name: EncLen
symbols.def: \(L(E)\) is the number of exact rational entries and discrete table cells in certificate \(E\).

symbols.name: LatProd
symbols.def: \(R(E)=\prod_{j=1}^{m(E)}|\mathcal U_j|\) is the number of joint latent assignments enumerated for certificate \(E\).

symbols.name: PS
symbols.def: \(P_{M,\sigma}^S(v)=P_M(V=v\mid S=1)\) for \(v\in\prod_{j\in V}\mathcal X_j\).

symbols.name: Theta
symbols.def: \(\Theta_{x,\sigma}(M)=P_M(Y\mid\operatorname{do}(X=x),S=1)\), with intervention applied before conditioning within signature \(\sigma\).

symbols.name: SComp
symbols.def: \(\operatorname{SComp}_{G^S}(H)\) is the partition induced on \(H\) by the districts of \(G^S[H\cup A_S\cup\{S\}]\).

symbols.name: I0
symbols.space: finite sets of nested S-component pairs
symbols.def: \(\mathcal I_0=\{(D_i,T_i^{(0)}):D_i\in\mathcal D_S(D),\ T_i^{(0)}\in\operatorname{SComp}_{G^S}(N_S),\ D_i\subseteq T_i^{(0)}\}\) is the family of calls made by Algorithm 1 before any recursion.

symbols.name: SHedge
symbols.def: \(\operatorname{SHedge}_{G^S}(C,T)\) is defined in \(\mathrm{def:s-hedge}\).

symbols.name: Ident
symbols.def: \(\operatorname{Ident}^{\mathrm{fin}}_S(G^S;X,Y)\) is defined in \(\mathrm{def:graphwise\text{-}sid}\) by quantifying over all finite signatures and all intervention values in each signature.

symbols.name: KSH
symbols.def: \(Q_{P_\sigma,x_N}^S[H]\) is the selected kernel generated from \(P_\sigma^S\) by the S-component decomposition and evaluated at \(X_N=x_N\) in every recursive factor.

symbols.name: Phi23
symbols.def: \(\Phi_{23,x}^{\sigma}(P_\sigma^S)\) is the signature- and intervention-indexed functional in Eq. 23 of AboueiEtAl2024LatentSID, with the outer conditional evaluated at \(X_S=x_S\) and every recursive selected kernel evaluated at \(X_N=x_N\).

symbols.name: PiS
symbols.def: \(\Pi_S(G^S)\) is the mixed graph on \(N_S\) defined in \(\mathrm{def:suppression\text{-}projection}\), with \(S\) included among the vertices permitted inside a suppressed path.

symbols.name: LiftHandle
symbols.def: \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{lift}}\) is the joint fiber-coupling route defined in \(\mathrm{def:inverse\text{-}lift\text{-}handle}\).

symbols.name: SHedgePair
symbols.def: \(\mathsf{SHedgePair}(G^S,C,T,x_{\mathrm{bin}};\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}})\) is the pair in \(\operatorname{CertSCM}(G^S,\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}})^2\) returned after the effective inverse lift and full-graph district extension.

symbols.name: AncestorPair
symbols.def: \(\mathsf{AncestorPair}(G^S,X,Y,x_{\mathrm{bin}};\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}})\) is the pair in \(\operatorname{CertSCM}(G^S,\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}})^2\) returned when the initial selected d-separation condition fails.

symbols.name: Rank
symbols.def: \(\rho\) records the cardinalities of the current enclosing S-components along the call chains rooted at \(\mathcal I_0\).

symbols.name: sIDplus
symbols.def: \(\mathsf{sID}^{\pm}\) augments the published Algorithm 1 with symbolic failure certificates.

symbols.name: Vstar
symbols.def: \(V_\star=\{B,D,Y,Z_1,Z_2\}\) is the substantive carrier of the two-virtual-edge instance.

symbols.name: Xstar
symbols.def: \(X_\star=\{B,D\}\) is the intervention set in the two-virtual-edge instance.

symbols.name: Ystar
symbols.def: \(Y_\star=\{Y\}\) is the outcome set in the two-virtual-edge instance.

symbols.name: sigmabinstar
symbols.def: \(\sigma_{\mathrm{bin},\star}=(\{0,1\})_{v\in V_\star\cup\{S\}}\) is the binary signature on the local carrier and selector.

symbols.name: xstar
symbols.def: \(x_\star\in\{0,1\}^{X_\star}\) is a local value assigned to \(X_\star\).

symbols.name: Gstar
symbols.def: \(G_\star^S\) has substantive carrier \(V_\star=\{B,D,Y,Z_1,Z_2\}\), directed edges \(B\to D\to Y\), \(Z_1\to S\), and \(Z_2\to S\), and bidirected edges \(D\leftrightarrow Z_1\leftrightarrow B\leftrightarrow Z_2\leftrightarrow Y\). The selector \(S\) is childless.

symbols.name: Mstarplus
symbols.space: sets of recursive augmented SCMs with arbitrary shared exogenous incidence
symbols.def: \(\mathfrak M_{\star,+}=\mathfrak M_+(G_\star^S,\sigma_{\mathrm{bin},\star})\) is the full positive compatible class on the local graph and signature.

symbols.name: Mstar0
symbols.def: \(M_{\star,0}\) is the first local model in the selected-law fiber comparison.

symbols.name: Mstar1
symbols.def: \(M_{\star,1}\) is the second local model in the selected-law fiber comparison.

symbols.name: Estar0
symbols.def: \(E_{\star,0}\) is the finite rational encoding whose realized model is \(M_{\star,0}=\llbracket E_{\star,0}\rrbracket\).

symbols.name: Estar1
symbols.def: \(E_{\star,1}\) is the finite rational encoding whose realized model is \(M_{\star,1}=\llbracket E_{\star,1}\rrbracket\).

symbols.name: Qstar
symbols.type: selected intervention on the early-kill graph
symbols.def: \(Q_{\star,x_\star}(M)=P_M(Y_\star\mid\operatorname{do}(X_\star=x_\star),S=1)\) for \(M\in\mathfrak M_{\star,+}\), with intervention applied before conditioning.

symbols.name: OTian
symbols.def: \(\mathcal O_{\mathrm{Tian}}=\{P(Z,A,L\mid S_E=1),P(Z,Y,L\mid S_I=1)\}\), where \(Z\) is the genetic instrument, \(A\) is HbA1c, \(Y\) is brain-age gap, \(L\) collects reported covariates, \(S_E\) denotes exposure-sample eligibility, and \(S_I\) denotes imaging-sample eligibility.

symbols.name: AuditTian
symbols.def: \(\mathsf{Audit}_{\mathrm{Tian}}\) records whether the two margins determine the single selected law required by \(\mathsf{sID}^{\pm}\), whether the relevant selected-sample IV independences hold, and whether Algorithm 1 succeeds on the declared graph.

assumptions.condition: For the fixed finite signature \(\sigma\), the generic model \(M\) is a recursive augmented SCM compatible with \(G^S\): its endogenous variable at \(v\) takes values in \(\mathcal X_v\), its exogenous variables are mutually independent, each exogenous variable may enter multiple endogenous mechanisms, every induced directed or pairwise bidirected adjacency is permitted by \(G^S\), and every listed edge may be inactive.

standard.name: recursive augmented-SCM compatibility with shared exogenous variables and a nonminimal graph

assumptions.condition: Within the fixed signature \(\sigma\), the generic model \(M\) satisfies \(P_M(V=v,S=1)>0\) for every \(v\in\prod_{j\in V}\mathcal X_j\).

definitions.name: positive compatible augmented-SCM class
definitions.construction: For every finite signature \(\sigma=(\mathcal X_v)_{v\in V\cup\{S\}}\) with \(2\le|\mathcal X_v|<\infty\) for \(v\in V\) and \(\mathcal X_S=\{0,1\}\), \(\mathfrak M_+(G^S,\sigma)=\{M:M\text{ has endogenous signature }\sigma,\ M\text{ is a recursive augmented SCM with mutually independent exogenous variables, each exogenous variable may enter multiple endogenous mechanisms, every induced adjacency is permitted by }G^S,\text{ and }P_M(V=v,S=1)>0\text{ for every }v\in\prod_{j\in V}\mathcal X_j\}\).

definitions.name: exact finite augmented-SCM certificate type
definitions.construction: \(\operatorname{CertSCM}(G^S,\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}})\) consists of finite strings \(E=((\mathcal U_j,p_j,I_j)_{j=1}^m,(f_v)_{v\in V\cup\{S\}})\). Each \(\mathcal U_j\) is a nonempty finite latent support, \(p_j:\mathcal U_j\to\mathbb Q\cap[0,1]\) is a complete normalized rational probability table, and \(I_j\subseteq V\cup\{S\}\) declares every endogenous mechanism receiving latent factor \(U_j\); distinct factors are interpreted independently with joint mass \(\prod_jp_j(u_j)\). Each \(f_v\) is a complete deterministic table from the declared observed-parent states and incident latent-factor states to \(\{0,1\}\). Every active observed-parent argument of \(f_v\) must be a permitted directed edge into \(v\) in \(G^S\), every pair of distinct vertices in an active scope \(I_j\) must have a permitted bidirected adjacency in \(G^S\), and the induced selected atom \(P_{\llbracket E\rrbracket}(V=v,S=1)\) must be positive for every \(v\in\{0,1\}^V\). A scope \(I_j\) may contain arbitrarily many mechanisms; permitted graph edges may remain inactive.

definitions.name: exact exhaustive NONID checker
definitions.construction: Given \(E_0,E_1\in\operatorname{CertSCM}(G^S,\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}})\) and \(x_{\mathrm{bin}}\), \(\mathsf{Check}_{\mathrm{NONID}}\) first validates finite-table completeness, the acyclicity of every active observed-parent relation, rational probability normalization and nonnegativity, the product-factor interpretation of mutual independence, and directed and shared-exogenous graph compatibility. For each \(i\in\{0,1\}\), exhaustive enumeration of the \(R(E_i)\) joint latent assignments computes exact unnormalized selected atoms \(a_i(v)=P_{\llbracket E_i\rrbracket}(V=v,S=1)\) and \(z_i=\sum_{v\in\{0,1\}^V}a_i(v)\). The checker requires \(a_i(v)>0\) and \(a_0(v)z_1=a_1(v)z_0\) for every \(v\in\{0,1\}^V\). It then replaces the structural tables for \(X\) by \(x_{\mathrm{bin}}\), enumerates again to obtain exact postintervention selected masses \(b_i(y)=P_{\llbracket E_i\rrbracket}(Y=y,S=1\mid\operatorname{do}(X=x_{\mathrm{bin}}))\) and \(q_i=\sum_{y\in\{0,1\}^Y}b_i(y)\), and accepts exactly when \(q_0q_1>0\) and \(b_0(y)q_1\ne b_1(y)q_0\) for some \(y\in\{0,1\}^Y\). For a universal implementation constant \(c\), this procedure uses at most \(c\{L(E_0)+L(E_1)+2^{|V|}(R(E_0)+R(E_1))(|V|+|Y|+1)\}\) exact rational arithmetic and table-lookup operations.

definitions.name: S-component partition
definitions.construction: For every \(H\subseteq N_S\), \(\operatorname{SComp}_{G^S}(H)=\{K\cap H:K\in\mathcal D(G^S[H\cup A_S\cup\{S\}]),\ K\cap H\ne\varnothing\}\), where \(\mathcal D\) denotes the district partition.

definitions.name: graphwise latent S-identification
definitions.construction: \(\operatorname{Ident}^{\mathrm{fin}}_S(G^S;X,Y)\iff\forall\sigma\ \forall x\in\prod_{v\in X}\mathcal X_v\ \forall M_0,M_1\in\mathfrak M_+(G^S,\sigma),\ P_{M_0,\sigma}^S=P_{M_1,\sigma}^S\Longrightarrow\Theta_{x,\sigma}(M_0)=\Theta_{x,\sigma}(M_1)\), where \(\sigma\) ranges over all finite signatures with at least two states for each substantive variable and binary \(S\). Models are compared only when they have the same signature \(\sigma\).

definitions.name: selected S-component kernel
definitions.construction: For a finite signature \(\sigma\) and \(H\subseteq N_S\), \(Q_{P_\sigma}^S[H]=(P_\sigma^S)_{N_S\setminus H}(H\mid A_S,S=1)\). The object \(Q_{P_\sigma,x_N}^S[H]\) denotes this kernel, and every kernel obtained from it by the published topological decomposition and recursive S-component marginalization, evaluated at the coordinates \(X_N=x_N\); all nonintervened arguments retain their displayed or summed values in \(\sigma\).

definitions.name: published Eq. 23 functional
definitions.construction: For every finite signature \(\sigma\) and every outcome value \(y=(y_S,y_N)\in\prod_{v\in Y}\mathcal X_v\), Eq. 23 is the pointwise functional \[\Phi_{23,x}^{\sigma}(P_\sigma^S)(y)=\sum_{w\in\mathcal X_W} P_\sigma^S(Y_S=y_S,W=w\mid X_S=x_S)\sum_{d_{D\setminus Y_N}\in\mathcal X_{D\setminus Y_N}}\prod_{D_i\in\mathcal D_S(D)}Q_{P_\sigma,x_N}^S[D_i]\bigl(d_i\mid y_S,w,x_S,d_{D\setminus D_i}\bigr).\] Every factor is produced by a successful single-component recursion and, at every recursion level, is evaluated at \(X_N=x_N\); the outer conditional is evaluated at \(X_S=x_S\).

definitions.name: selection-ancestor suppression projection
definitions.construction: \(\Pi_S(G^S)\) has vertex set \(N_S\), inherits every directed edge of \(G^S[N_S]\), and has \(u\leftrightarrow v\) exactly when \(G^S\) contains a bidirected path from \(u\) to \(v\) whose internal vertices all lie in \(A_S\cup\{S\}\).

definitions.name: joint fiber-coupling inverse-lift handle
definitions.construction: For a terminal call descended from \(\operatorname{sID\text{-}Single}(D_i,T_i^{(0)},Q_{P_{\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}}}}^S[T_i^{(0)}])\) with \(C=D_i\subsetneq T\subseteq T_i^{(0)}\) and \(\operatorname{SHedge}_{G^S}(C,T)\), \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{lift}}\) starts from an ordinary positive rational hedge pair on \(\Pi_S(G^S)[T]\) under \(\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}}\). It collects in one incidence hypergraph every original bidirected path through \(A_S\cup\{S\}\) that realizes a virtual edge, introduces jointly rational parameters of mutually independent finite latent factors that may each enter several endogenous mechanisms and all ancestor mechanisms, imposes equality of every binary-signature selected atom before normalization together with preservation of the projected hedge kernels, eliminates shared or branching ancestor mechanisms in a topological order, and searches the remaining rational nullspace for a direction with nonzero target contrast. Its target object is an effective inverse-lift constructor producing \(E_0,E_1\in\operatorname{CertSCM}(G^S[T\cup A_S\cup\{S\}],\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}})\), with accepted exact checker evidence and realized models in the full class \(\mathfrak M_+(G^S,\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}})\).

definitions.name: S-Hedge countermodel certificate
definitions.construction: For a terminal Algorithm 1 trace rooted at \(D_i\in\mathcal D_S(D)\), with initial enclosure \(T_i^{(0)}\), fixed target \(C=D_i\), terminal enclosure \(C\subsetneq T\subseteq T_i^{(0)}\), and \(\operatorname{SHedge}_{G^S}(C,T)\), \(\mathsf{SHedgePair}(G^S,C,T,x_{\mathrm{bin}};\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}})=(E_0,E_1)\) is the exact rational pair in \(\operatorname{CertSCM}(G^S,\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}})^2\) obtained by applying the effective joint fiber-coupling inverse lift to an ordinary rational parity hedge pair at \(x_{\mathrm{bin}}\) on \(\Pi_S(G^S)[T]\) and applying a rational district-extension operation to all vertices outside the failed component. The returned object includes evidence that \(\mathsf{Check}_{\mathrm{NONID}}(G^S,X,Y,x_{\mathrm{bin}},E_0,E_1)=\mathrm{accept}\).

definitions.name: initial-call family and size-sum budget
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal I_0=\{(D_i,T_i^{(0)}):D_i\in\mathcal D_S(D),\ T_i^{(0)}\in\operatorname{SComp}_{G^S}(N_S),\ D_i\subseteq T_i^{(0)}\}\), where \(T_i^{(0)}\) is the unique S-component of \(N_S\) containing \(D_i\), and \(B_0=\sum_{(D_i,T_i^{(0)})\in\mathcal I_0}|T_i^{(0)}|\).

definitions.name: initial d-separation failure certificate
definitions.construction: \(\mathsf{AncestorPair}(G^S,X,Y,x_{\mathrm{bin}};\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}})=(E_0,E_1)\) applies the positive rational binary countermodel construction from the complete fully observed S-ID necessity proof on \(A_S\cup\{S\}\), records every finite latent support, rational mass table, incidence scope, and deterministic structural table in \(\operatorname{CertSCM}(G^S,\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}})\), and sets all permitted bidirected edges and all nonancestor mechanisms outside that construction inactive and common. The returned object includes evidence that \(\mathsf{Check}_{\mathrm{NONID}}(G^S,X,Y,x_{\mathrm{bin}},E_0,E_1)=\mathrm{accept}\).

definitions.name: multiset recursion rank
definitions.construction: For the call chains rooted at \(\mathcal I_0\), let \(T_i^{(r)}\) be the current enclosure on root \(i\), with fixed target \(C=D_i\). The rank is \(\rho=\{\!\{|T_i^{(r)}|:i\text{ active}\}\!\}\), ordered by the well-founded multiset extension of \(<\) on \(\mathbb N\). A recursive step replaces \(T_i^{(r)}\) by the S-component \(T_i^{(r+1)}\subseteq\operatorname{An}_{G^S[T_i^{(r)}]}(D_i)\subsetneq T_i^{(r)}\) containing \(D_i\).

definitions.name: executable S-ID success-or-certificate algorithm
definitions.construction: \(\mathsf{sID}^{\pm}\) runs published Algorithm 1 on a finite augmented ADMG in which \(S\) has no children and records \(\mathcal I_0\). Given any finite signature \(\sigma\), on success at intervention value \(x\in\mathcal X_X\) it returns \(\operatorname{ID}(\Phi_{23,x}^{\sigma})\). If the initial d-separation check fails it chooses \(x_{\mathrm{bin}}\in\{0,1\}^{X}\) and returns \(\operatorname{NONID}(x_{\mathrm{bin}},E_0,E_1,\mathsf{Check}_{\mathrm{NONID}}=\mathrm{accept};\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}})\), where \((E_0,E_1)=\mathsf{AncestorPair}(G^S,X,Y,x_{\mathrm{bin}};\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}})\). If the call rooted at \(D_i\in\mathcal D_S(D)\) reaches a terminal failure \(\operatorname{sID\text{-}Single}(C,T,Q_{P_\sigma}^S[T])\), then \(C=D_i\), \(C\subsetneq T\subseteq T_i^{(0)}\), both \(C\) and \(T\) are single S-components, and \(\operatorname{An}_{G^S[T]}(C)=T\); the algorithm chooses \(x_{\mathrm{bin}}\) and returns the same encoded \(\operatorname{NONID}\) object with \((E_0,E_1)=\mathsf{SHedgePair}(G^S,C,T,x_{\mathrm{bin}};\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}})\). This total failure branch is enabled only by a proved effective inverse-lift constructor returning rational \(\operatorname{CertSCM}\) objects; an existential arbitrary-SCM lift does not implement \(\mathsf{sID}^{\pm}\). The trace stores the multiset rank before and after every recursive call.

definitions.name: two-virtual-edge early-kill instance
definitions.construction: On \(V_\star=\{B,D,Y,Z_1,Z_2\}\), set \(X_\star=\{B,D\}\), \(Y_\star=\{Y\}\), and \(\sigma_{\mathrm{bin},\star}=(\{0,1\})_{v\in V_\star\cup\{S\}}\). For \(x_\star\in\{0,1\}^{X_\star}\), the early-kill calculation eliminates exact rational response-type parameters over \(E_{\star,0},E_{\star,1}\in\operatorname{CertSCM}(G_\star^S,\sigma_{\mathrm{bin},\star})\), with \(M_{\star,i}=\llbracket E_{\star,i}\rrbracket\in\mathfrak M_{\star,+}\), subject to \(P_{M_{\star,0}}(V_\star=v\mid S=1)=P_{M_{\star,1}}(V_\star=v\mid S=1)>0\) for every \(v\in\{0,1\}^{V_\star}\), and tests whether \(Q_{\star,x_\star}(M_{\star,0})\ne Q_{\star,x_\star}(M_{\star,1})\) is feasible. A separating pair must also satisfy the local instance of \(\mathsf{Check}_{\mathrm{NONID}}=\mathrm{accept}\). The local instance is embedded in the generic notation by substituting \(V_\star,G_\star^S,X_\star,Y_\star,\sigma_{\mathrm{bin},\star},x_\star,E_{\star,0},E_{\star,1},M_{\star,0},M_{\star,1}\) for \(V,G^S,X,Y,\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}},x_{\mathrm{bin}},E_0,E_1,M_0,M_1\), respectively.

definitions.name: Tian two-sample input
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal O_{\mathrm{Tian}}=\{P(Z,A,L\mid S_E=1),P(Z,Y,L\mid S_I=1)\}\), with the two selectors and measured margins kept distinct.

definitions.name: UK Biobank selected-law audit
definitions.construction: \(\mathsf{Audit}_{\mathrm{Tian}}(\mathcal O_{\mathrm{Tian}},G^S)\) returns four entries: whether a common full selected law is identified from the two margins; whether \(Z\) is independent of latent HbA1c--brain-aging causes after each selection event; whether intervention on \(A\) is evaluated before imaging and eligibility conditioning; and whether \(\mathsf{sID}^{\pm}\) returns \(\operatorname{ID}\) or a countermodel certificate for the declared selected-subpopulation target.

statements.statement: For every finite signature \(\sigma\), every \(M\in\mathfrak M_+(G^S,\sigma)\), and every \(x\in\prod_{v\in X}\mathcal X_v\), strict selected-cell positivity on \(\prod_{v\in V}\mathcal X_v\) and SCM consistency imply \(P_M(S=1\mid\operatorname{do}(X=x))>0\). Hence \(\Theta_{x,\sigma}(M)\) is defined without an additional postintervention support assumption.
statements.justification: This removes a redundant support premise while keeping intervention-before-conditioning mathematically defined.
statements.gap: AboueiEtAl2024LatentSID assumes a strictly positive selected observational law but does not isolate this consistency consequence as a separate lemma.
statements.consumer: Every graphwise comparison and every finite-binary failure certificate can use the selected intervention target without strengthening the published model class.

statements.statement: Every encoding \(E\in\operatorname{CertSCM}(G^S,\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}})\) realizes a recursive augmented SCM \(\llbracket E\rrbracket\in\mathfrak M_+(G^S,\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}})\). Its finite latent factors are mutually independent by their product law, a factor may feed any number of mechanisms, every active induced directed or pairwise bidirected adjacency is permitted by \(G^S\), permitted edges may be inactive, and every selected atom is positive. Hence \(\operatorname{CertSCM}(G^S,\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}})\subseteq\mathfrak M_+(G^S,\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}})\) under the realization map, without restricting the ambient graphwise identification quantifier.
statements.justification: This separates a finitely checkable witness language from the unrestricted model class over which identification is defined.
statements.gap: AboueiEtAl2024LatentSID permits shared exogenous variables but does not define a finite exact syntax for countermodels or prove its interpretation compatible with that class.
statements.consumer: Every accepted encoded NONID object becomes a valid counterexample to graphwise identification in the full published augmented-SCM class.

statements.statement: For \(E_0,E_1\in\operatorname{CertSCM}(G^S,\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}})\), if \(\mathsf{Check}_{\mathrm{NONID}}(G^S,X,Y,x_{\mathrm{bin}},E_0,E_1)=\mathrm{accept}\), then the realized models lie in \(\mathfrak M_+(G^S,\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}})\), satisfy \(P_{\llbracket E_0\rrbracket,\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}}}^S=P_{\llbracket E_1\rrbracket,\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}}}^S>0\) on every binary cell, and satisfy \(\Theta_{x_{\mathrm{bin}},\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}}}(\llbracket E_0\rrbracket)\ne\Theta_{x_{\mathrm{bin}},\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}}}(\llbracket E_1\rrbracket)\). The checker terminates after at most \(c\{L(E_0)+L(E_1)+2^{|V|}(R(E_0)+R(E_1))(|V|+|Y|+1)\}\) exact rational arithmetic and table-lookup operations for a universal implementation constant \(c\).
statements.justification: The failure branch is reproducible only when finite syntax, exact equality, target separation, and an explicit enumeration bound are certified together.
statements.gap: Neither latent S-ID nor ordinary hedge completeness supplies an exact certificate checker for normalized selected-law equality under shared exogenous incidence.
statements.consumer: Independent software can validate a returned failure witness without trusting the inverse-lift implementation.

statements.statement: For every \(H\subseteq N_S\), the districts of \(\Pi_S(G^S)[H]\) are exactly \(\operatorname{SComp}_{G^S}(H)\). More precisely, two vertices of \(H\) are bidirected-connected in \(G^S[H\cup A_S\cup\{S\}]\) if and only if they are bidirected-connected in \(\Pi_S(G^S)[H]\).
statements.justification: This establishes that S-components are ordinary districts after the precise suppression operation.
statements.gap: AboueiEtAl2024LatentSID defines S-components through ancestors of selection but does not state this projection equivalence.
statements.consumer: The ordinary hedge countermodel theorem of ShpitserPearl2006 can be invoked only after this graph-level correspondence is certified.

statements.statement: For every finite signature \(\sigma\), fix \(D_i\in\mathcal D_S(D)\), let \(T_i^{(0)}\) be the unique member of \(\operatorname{SComp}_{G^S}(N_S)\) containing \(D_i\), and consider the call chain of \(\operatorname{sID\text{-}Single}(D_i,T_i^{(0)},Q_{P_\sigma}^S[T_i^{(0)}])\). If this chain fails at \((C,T)\), then \(C=D_i\), \(C\subsetneq T\subseteq T_i^{(0)}\), \(\operatorname{SComp}_{G^S}(C)=\{C\}\), \(\operatorname{SComp}_{G^S}(T)=\{T\}\), and \(\operatorname{An}_{G^S[T]}(C)=T\). Consequently \(\operatorname{SHedge}_{G^S}(C,T)\), while each of \(\Pi_S(G^S)[C]\) and \(\Pi_S(G^S)[T]\) has one district, so \((C,T)\) has the ordinary Shpitser--Pearl hedge geometry. Within such a terminal call, these displayed conditions are equivalent to the S-Hedge predicate.
statements.justification: The equivalence localizes the new completeness work to realization of virtual bidirected edges rather than to a new hedge combinatorics.
statements.gap: ShpitserPearl2006 treats ordinary districts, whereas AboueiEtAl2024LatentSID leaves the relationship between S-Hedges and ordinary hedge geometry implicit.
statements.consumer: It supplies the projected counterpair input to the inverse-lift question.

statements.statement: Let \(V_\star=\{B,D,Y,Z_1,Z_2\}\), \(X_\star=\{B,D\}\), \(Y_\star=\{Y\}\), and let \(\sigma_{\mathrm{bin},\star}\) be binary on \(V_\star\cup\{S\}\). The exact rational response-type elimination for the fixed graph \(G_\star^S\), whose selector \(S\) is childless, has a strictly positive selected-law fiber on which the local target is nonconstant: there exist \(x_\star\in\{0,1\}^{X_\star}\) and \(E_{\star,0},E_{\star,1}\in\operatorname{CertSCM}(G_\star^S,\sigma_{\mathrm{bin},\star})\), with realized models \(M_{\star,i}=\llbracket E_{\star,i}\rrbracket\in\mathfrak M_{\star,+}\), such that \[P_{M_{\star,0}}(V_\star=v\mid S=1)=P_{M_{\star,1}}(V_\star=v\mid S=1)>0\quad\text{for every }v\in\{0,1\}^{V_\star},\] \(Q_{\star,x_\star}(M_{\star,0})\ne Q_{\star,x_\star}(M_{\star,1})\), and the local exact checker accepts. Their finite latent factors may each enter multiple endogenous mechanisms and permitted edges may be inactive. Under the substitution \(V=V_\star\), \(G^S=G_\star^S\), \(X=X_\star\), \(Y=Y_\star\), \(\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}}=\sigma_{\mathrm{bin},\star}\), \(x_{\mathrm{bin}}=x_\star\), \(E_i=E_{\star,i}\), and \(M_i=M_{\star,i}\), this pair is a local instance of the generic encoded failure certificate and its realization in the full class.
statements.justification: This is the smallest shared-incidence calculation that must exhibit a nonconstant target fiber before any universal inverse-lift claim is credible.
statements.gap: AboueiEtAl2024LatentSID returns an S-Hedge failure on the relevant geometry but does not calculate this selected-law fiber or produce its two rational points.
statements.consumer: The universal inverse-lift question is pursued only after this lemma certifies that two interacting virtual edges do not force target constancy.

statements.statement: Can the joint fiber-coupling handle \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{lift}}\) be completed as an effective exact-rational constructor so that, for every finite augmented ADMG \(G^S\) in which \(S\) has no children, every \(D_i\in\mathcal D_S(D)\), and every terminal failed call descended from \(\operatorname{sID\text{-}Single}(D_i,T_i^{(0)},Q_{P_{\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}}}}^S[T_i^{(0)}])\) at \((C,T)\), where \(T_i^{(0)}\in\operatorname{SComp}_{G^S}(N_S)\), \(C=D_i\subsetneq T\subseteq T_i^{(0)}\), \(\operatorname{SComp}_{G^S}(C)=\{C\}\), \(\operatorname{SComp}_{G^S}(T)=\{T\}\), and \(\operatorname{An}_{G^S[T]}(C)=T\), it lifts every positive rational ordinary hedge pair on \(\Pi_S(G^S)[T]\) under \(\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}}\) to \(E_0,E_1\in\operatorname{CertSCM}(G^S,\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}})\)? The realized models \(M_i=\llbracket E_i\rrbracket\) must belong to the full published class \(\mathfrak M_+(G^S,\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}})\), permit each mutually independent finite latent factor to enter multiple endogenous mechanisms, preserve the projected local kernels at \(X_N=x_{\mathrm{bin}}|_{X_N}\), and satisfy \(\mathsf{Check}_{\mathrm{NONID}}(G^S,X,Y,x_{\mathrm{bin}},E_0,E_1)=\mathrm{accept}\) for some returned \(x_{\mathrm{bin}}\in\{0,1\}^{X}\). The handle must couple all shared and branching selection-ancestor paths jointly and must output the finite supports, rational probability tables, incidence scopes, and deterministic structural tables, using the accepted nonconstant fiber of \(Q_{\star,x_\star}\) on \((V_\star,G_\star^S,X_\star,Y_\star,\sigma_{\mathrm{bin},\star})\) as its first compositional base case.
statements.justification: Shared and branching ancestors couple structural equations and the selection normalizer, so this is the nonroutine step separating the conjecture from ordinary ID completeness.
statements.gap: ShpitserPearl2006 constructs ordinary hedge pairs, ChenZoeterMooij2024 controls forward conditioning operations, and KivvaEtAl2023 supplies positive finite separators, but none gives this inverse realization with a fixed normalized selected law.
statements.consumer: A positive answer closes the necessity direction for every actual recursive failure; failure beyond the certified two-virtual-edge base case identifies the incidence restriction needed for the maximal completeness class.

statements.statement: Fix \(D_i\in\mathcal D_S(D)\) and its initial enclosure \(T_i^{(0)}\in\operatorname{SComp}_{G^S}(N_S)\). For a call chain with fixed target \(C=D_i\) that ends at a terminal failure \(C\subsetneq T\subseteq T_i^{(0)}\) satisfying \(\operatorname{SHedge}_{G^S}(C,T)\), any local exact rational pair supplied by the effective \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{lift}}\) extends through the selected district factorization to \(\mathsf{SHedgePair}(G^S,C,T,x_{\mathrm{bin}};\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}})=(E_0,E_1)\in\operatorname{CertSCM}(G^S,\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}})^2\). The extension appends identical rational strictly positive kernels outside the failed component and preserves arbitrary permitted shared-exogenous incidence. It yields \(\mathsf{Check}_{\mathrm{NONID}}(G^S,X,Y,x_{\mathrm{bin}},E_0,E_1)=\mathrm{accept}\); consequently the realized models \(M_i=\llbracket E_i\rrbracket\in\mathfrak M_+(G^S,\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}})\) have one positive selected law and unequal targets.
statements.justification: A local kernel contrast is not yet a counterexample for the full target until equality and separation survive every other district.
statements.gap: TianPearl2002 and ShpitserPearl2006 provide ordinary district lifting; the selected normalization and ancestor block make the required extension different.
statements.consumer: It converts a terminal Algorithm 1 trace into a complete, checkable nonidentification certificate for the original query.

statements.statement: For every finite augmented ADMG \(G^S\) in which \(S\) has no children and every disjoint \(X,Y\subseteq V\) with \(Y\ne\varnothing\), published Algorithm 1 succeeds on the graph query \((G^S,X,Y)\) if and only if \(\operatorname{Ident}^{\mathrm{fin}}_S(G^S;X,Y)\) holds over all finite signatures \(\sigma=(\mathcal X_v)_{v\in V\cup\{S\}}\) satisfying \(2\le|\mathcal X_v|<\infty\) for every \(v\in V\) and \(\mathcal X_S=\{0,1\}\), where each observational-equivalence comparison uses two models in the same unrestricted class \(\mathfrak M_+(G^S,\sigma)\) and mutually independent exogenous variables may each enter multiple endogenous mechanisms. On success, for every such \(\sigma\), every \(x\in\prod_{v\in X}\mathcal X_v\), and every \(M\in\mathfrak M_+(G^S,\sigma)\) inducing \(P_{M,\sigma}^S\), the output evaluated at \(x_S=x|_{X_S}\) and \(x_N=x|_{X_N}\) satisfies \(\Phi_{23,x}^{\sigma}(P_{M,\sigma}^S)=\Theta_{x,\sigma}(M)\) pointwise in \(x\). If the initial d-separation check fails, the certificate chooses \(x_{\mathrm{bin}}\) and returns \((E_0,E_1)=\mathsf{AncestorPair}(G^S,X,Y,x_{\mathrm{bin}};\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}})\in\operatorname{CertSCM}(G^S,\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}})^2\) with accepted checker evidence. Otherwise Algorithm 1 forms \(\mathcal D_S(D)=\{D_1,\ldots,D_k\}\) and, for each \(D_i\), starts \(\operatorname{sID\text{-}Single}(D_i,T_i^{(0)},Q_{P_\sigma}^S[T_i^{(0)}])\), where \(T_i^{(0)}\) is the unique member of \(\operatorname{SComp}_{G^S}(N_S)\) containing \(D_i\). If that call chain fails terminally at \((C,T)\), then \(C=D_i\subsetneq T\subseteq T_i^{(0)}\), \(\operatorname{SComp}_{G^S}(C)=\{C\}\), \(\operatorname{SComp}_{G^S}(T)=\{T\}\), and \(\operatorname{An}_{G^S[T]}(C)=T\), hence \(\operatorname{SHedge}_{G^S}(C,T)\), and the certificate chooses \(x_{\mathrm{bin}}\) and returns \((E_0,E_1)=\mathsf{SHedgePair}(G^S,C,T,x_{\mathrm{bin}};\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}})\in\operatorname{CertSCM}(G^S,\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}})^2\) with \(\mathsf{Check}_{\mathrm{NONID}}=\mathrm{accept}\). In either failure branch, \(M_i=\llbracket E_i\rrbracket\) lies in the full shared-exogenous class \(\mathfrak M_+(G^S,\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}})\), the selected laws are equal and positive, and the targets differ. This is a strict extension of the fully observed S-ID theorem because it also covers childless-selector augmented ADMGs with active bidirected edges.
statements.justification: This resolves the explicit completeness conjecture and makes every algorithmic failure as informative as every success.
statements.gap: AboueiEtAl2024LatentSID proves soundness and conjectures the converse; ShpitserPearl2006 proves the analogous ordinary-ID result without selection ancestors or normalized selected-law equivalence.
statements.consumer: Graphical analysts obtain a definitive answer for any latent selected-subpopulation query and a concrete falsifying pair whenever point identification fails.

statements.statement: Assume the joint fiber-coupling handle is proved to be an effective constructor returning rational \(\operatorname{CertSCM}\) pairs with accepted checker evidence for every actual terminal Algorithm 1 failure. Then, for every finite augmented ADMG \(G^S\) in which \(S\) has no children, every finite signature \(\sigma\), and every \(x\in\prod_{v\in X}\mathcal X_v\), \(\mathsf{sID}^{\pm}\) is total. It returns either \(\operatorname{ID}(\Phi_{23,x}^{\sigma})\) or \(\operatorname{NONID}(x_{\mathrm{bin}},E_0,E_1,\mathsf{Check}_{\mathrm{NONID}}=\mathrm{accept};\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}})\). Its initial call family is \(\mathcal I_0=\{(D_i,T_i^{(0)}):D_i\in\mathcal D_S(D)\}\). Along the chain rooted at \((D_i,T_i^{(0)})\), the target remains \(C=D_i\); a recursive step forms \(A=\operatorname{An}_{G^S[T]}(D_i)\) and replaces \(T\) by the S-component \(T'\subseteq A\subsetneq T\) containing \(D_i\). Thus \(\rho\) decreases strictly. The chain rooted at \(T_i^{(0)}\) contains at most \(|T_i^{(0)}|\) single-component invocations, the recursion depth is at most \(\max_i|T_i^{(0)}|\le|N_S|\), and the total number of single-component invocations is at most \(B_0=\sum_{(D_i,T_i^{(0)})\in\mathcal I_0}|T_i^{(0)}|\). For each returned NONID pair, the exact checker terminates within \(c\{L(E_0)+L(E_1)+2^{|V|}(R(E_0)+R(E_1))(|V|+|Y|+1)\}\) rational arithmetic and table-lookup operations and certifies that the realized models are members of the full shared-exogenous class with equal positive selected laws and unequal targets. An existential witness in an arbitrary SCM representation does not establish this totality claim.
statements.justification: Completeness is operational only if both outputs are checkable and the recursive search has a transparent finite bound.
statements.gap: AboueiEtAl2024LatentSID gives a terminating sound identifier but no failure-model compiler or certificate checker.
statements.consumer: Software implementing latent S-ID can expose either the published formula or a reproducible binary counterexample rather than an uninterpreted failure flag.

statements.statement: If \(G^S\) has no bidirected edges and \(S\) has no children, then every S-component is a singleton, no recursive S-Hedge exists, and \(\mathsf{sID}^{\pm}\) reduces to the sound-and-complete fully observed S-ID criterion of AboueiEtAl2024SID. For every finite signature \(\sigma\) and pointwise for every \(x\in\prod_{v\in X}\mathcal X_v\), its initial d-separation condition and its returned functional \(\Phi_{23,x}^{\sigma}\) agree with that published criterion.
statements.justification: The latent-free special case is the required sanity reduction and guards against changing the meaning of selected-subpopulation intervention.
statements.gap: AboueiEtAl2024SID settles the DAG case; the proposition verifies exact agreement rather than offering a new DAG result.
statements.consumer: Existing fully observed S-ID implementations become regression tests for the augmented algorithm.

statements.statement: For the two-sample input \(\mathcal O_{\mathrm{Tian}}\), a claim identifying \(P_A(Y\mid S_I=1)\) by latent S-ID is valid only after \(\mathsf{Audit}_{\mathrm{Tian}}\) certifies a common full selected-law input and \(\mathsf{sID}^{\pm}\) returns \(\operatorname{ID}\) on the declared augmented graph. Population IV relevance, independence, exclusion, and horizontal-pleiotropy checks alone do not imply the selected-sample independence \(Z\mathbin{\perp\!\!\!\perp}U\mid S_I=1\) or equality of the exposure-sample and imaging-sample selection mechanisms. If the audit returns \(\operatorname{NONID}(x_{\mathrm{bin}},E_0,E_1,\mathsf{Check}_{\mathrm{NONID}}=\mathrm{accept})\), the realized models \(\llbracket E_0\rrbracket,\llbracket E_1\rrbracket\) agree on the audited selected input and disagree on the selected intervention target.
statements.justification: The UK Biobank analysis uses two differently selected samples, so the observed input and selected estimand must be stated before graphical identification can be claimed.
statements.gap: TianEtAl2024HbA1c reports standard Mendelian-randomization checks but no augmented selection graph, while TyrrellEtAl2021, LyallEtAl2022, and SchoelerEtAl2023 document systematic participation and imaging selection.
statements.consumer: Researchers reanalyzing HbA1c and brain aging obtain an explicit ledger of additional data-fusion and selected-sample independence assumptions, together with a countermodel when those assumptions are insufficient.

sampling_model.design: Population graphical identification is required uniformly over all finite signatures \(\sigma\) from one exact selected observational law within each signature; no randomization or sampling approximation is used in the completeness theorem.
sampling_model.units: A generic recursive augmented SCM on a finite ADMG \(G^S\) whose selection node \(S\) has no children, with \(2\le|\mathcal X_v|<\infty\) for each substantive variable and binary \(S\); mutually independent exogenous variables may each enter multiple endogenous mechanisms. Identification ranges over this full class. A returned failure witness uses \(\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}}\) and an exact finite rational \(\operatorname{CertSCM}\) encoding whose realized model is proved to belong to the full class.
sampling_model.treatment: For each signature, \(x\in\prod_{v\in X}\mathcal X_v\), and the intervention \(\operatorname{do}(X=x)\) is applied to the SCM before conditioning on \(S=1\).
sampling_model.overlap: Within each signature, every cell \(v\in\prod_{j\in V}\mathcal X_j\) has \(P_M(V=v,S=1)>0\), and the queried postintervention selection event has positive probability.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: None. Within each signature the input is the exact law \(P_{M,\sigma}^S=P_M(V\mid S=1)\); estimation of Eq. 23 is a separate statistical problem.

estimand_functional: \(\Phi_{23,x}^{\sigma}(P_\sigma^S)(y)=\sum_{w\in\mathcal X_W} P_\sigma^S(Y_S=y_S,W=w\mid X_S=x_S)\sum_{d_{D\setminus Y_N}\in\mathcal X_{D\setminus Y_N}}\prod_{D_i\in\mathcal D_S(D)}Q_{P_\sigma,x_N}^S[D_i](d_i\mid y_S,w,x_S,d_{D\setminus D_i})\)

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Algorithm 1 and Eq. 23 are sound for latent S-ID, while completeness is left as a conjecture.
The fully observed augmented-DAG S-ID criterion is sound and complete.
Ordinary semi-Markovian ID is complete, with hedges certifying algorithmic failure.
The Tian--Pearl identification recursion is complete for ordinary semi-Markovian causal effects.
Conditioning an SCM on latent selection preserves causal semantics and commutes with intervention outside the selector's ancestors.
Positive finite countermodels establish completeness for conditional generalized identification.
Discrete causal questions with selection admit sharp polynomial-program bounds over canonical response types.
Full-population ATE recovery from selected data has a necessary-and-sufficient distribution-class condition under unconfoundedness.
A two-sample Mendelian-randomization analysis studies HbA1c and white-matter brain aging in differently selected UK Biobank samples.

tldr: Latent S-ID currently has a sound recursive algorithm but no graphwise converse over the published childless-selector augmented-SCM class, in which one independent exogenous variable may enter several mechanisms. The proposal proves that, for an actual terminal Algorithm 1 call rooted at an Eq. 23 factor \(D_i\), both the fixed target \(C=D_i\) and the terminal enclosure \(T\) are single S-components and suppressing bidirected paths internal to ancestors of selection converts their S-Hedge into ordinary hedge geometry. An exact two-virtual-edge selected-law fiber separation is the mandatory first lemma before the open compositional inverse lift. Resolving that lift yields a necessary-and-sufficient theorem uniformly over every finite signature \(\sigma=(\mathcal X_v)\) with at least two states per substantive variable and binary \(S\): within each fixed signature and pointwise in \(x\), Algorithm 1 returns \(\Phi_{23,x}^{\sigma}(P_{M,\sigma}^S)=\Theta_{x,\sigma}(M)\) exactly on graphwise identified queries. A failure returns two exact finite rational \(\operatorname{CertSCM}\) encodings with shared latent scopes allowed, accepted checker evidence, one positive selected law, and unequal targets; their realizations lie in the unrestricted published class. A multiset rank and the initial size-sum budget certify graph recursion, while executable totality additionally requires the open inverse lift to be an effective certificate constructor. The latent-free restriction recovers published complete S-ID, and a separate audit states what the two UK Biobank samples must establish before the HbA1c-to-brain-aging analysis can be interpreted as a selected-subpopulation intervention.

project_justification.gap: AboueiEtAl2024LatentSID proves Algorithm 1 sound and explicitly leaves completeness open. Ordinary hedge completeness does not preserve a normalized selected law when several virtual bidirected edges share or branch through ancestors of \(S\), and no published inverse-lift theorem supplies that missing equality-preserving construction.
project_justification.niche: For each Eq. 23 factor \(D_i\), the terminal recursion keeps the single-S-component target \(C=D_i\) fixed while strictly shrinking its single-S-component enclosure. The suppression projection isolates the resulting ordinary hedge while retaining a finite incidence structure that records how its virtual edges are realized inside \(\operatorname{An}(S)\).
project_justification.fill: The project first proves nonconstancy of the exact binary-signature selected-law fiber on the two-virtual-edge kill graph, then proves the terminal-call projection correspondence, derives an effective rational joint inverse lift, extends the encoded local witness through selected district factorization, and packages the result as a success-or-certificate algorithm. The success claim is uniform over all finite signatures with at least two states per substantive variable. Each failure output is a finite rational table encoding with arbitrary finite shared-latent scopes, exact checker evidence, and a proved realization in the full published model class. The total graph call count is bounded by the sum of the initial enclosing-component sizes, and the checker has an explicit exhaustive-enumeration operation bound.

related_work: AboueiEtAl2024LatentSID supplies the exact childless-selector augmented-SCM setup, allows each mutually independent exogenous variable to be shared by several endogenous mechanisms, defines S-components and S-Hedges, and gives Algorithm 1 and Eq. 23; its soundness theorem is the sufficiency half, and its explicit completeness conjecture is the target. ShpitserPearl2006 and HuangValtorta2008 prove ordinary semi-Markovian ID completeness by localizing failure to hedge geometry and lifting binary countermodels through c-components. TianPearl2002 supplies the district factorization used by both algorithms. AboueiEtAl2024SID proves the fully observed selected-subpopulation criterion and provides the required no-bidirected-edge reduction under a childless selector. ChenZoeterMooij2024 proves that selection conditioning is a causal SCM transformation and that intervention commutes with it away from ancestors of selection, but it does not invert the transformation or preserve a common selected law across countermodels. KivvaEtAl2023 shows how positivity can be retained in finite nonidentification constructions through a global linear-algebra perturbation; its construction is not a binary S-Hedge lift. RichardsonEtAl2017 formalizes latent projection and nested district kernels, which provide the language for the full-graph extension. DuarteEtAl2024AutoBounds gives a general polynomial program for discrete partial identification with selection, but it neither proves singleton collapse exactly at latent S-ID success nor supplies an analytic S-Hedge certificate. QiuEtAl2026 characterizes full-population ATE recovery over restricted propensity, outcome, and selection classes under unconfoundedness; it does not subsume graphwise selected interventional identification in the published augmented-SCM class. BhattacharyaNabiShpitser2022 addresses estimation after ordinary hidden-variable identification, not the graphwise converse. TianEtAl2024HbA1c motivates the application audit, while TyrrellEtAl2021, LyallEtAl2022, and SchoelerEtAl2023 document selection mechanisms capable of invalidating population MR independences after UK Biobank participation and imaging selection.
technical_internal_limitation: The unresolved obstruction is simultaneous realization when virtual-edge paths share or branch through ancestors of \(S\): changing one ancestor mechanism can change every selected atom and its normalizer. The exact response-type elimination on the local instance \((V_\star,G_\star^S,X_\star,Y_\star,\sigma_{\mathrm{bin},\star})\) is therefore a kill condition, not an illustration. If its common positive selected-law fiber on \(\{0,1\}^{V_\star}\) is constant in \(Q_{\star,x_\star}\) for every \(x_\star\in\{0,1\}^{X_\star}\), the universal inverse lift is false; the headline must then become completeness on the maximal incidence class supported by the calculation, together with a proved inclusion relation to the published graph class. The universal theorem depends on the nonconstant-fiber lemma and does not bypass it.
honest_scope: The headline is graphwise population identification uniformly over all finite signatures \(\sigma=(\mathcal X_v)_{v\in V\cup\{S\}}\) with \(2\le|\mathcal X_v|<\infty\) for substantive variables and \(\mathcal X_S=\{0,1\}\). Observational equivalence compares models only within the same signature. The ambient model class is the published childless-selector augmented-SCM class with mutually independent exogenous variables allowed to enter multiple mechanisms and inactive permitted edges; it is not restricted to finitely encoded or one-latent-per-edge models. The functional \(\Phi_{23,x}^{\sigma}\) is evaluated at \(X_S=x_S\) in the outer conditional and at \(X_N=x_N\) throughout every recursive selected kernel, and equals \(\Theta_{x,\sigma}\) pointwise in \(x\) on success. Postintervention selection support is derived within each signature from selected-cell positivity and SCM consistency. Only returned nonidentification witnesses lie in the exact rational type \(\operatorname{CertSCM}(G^S,\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}})\), whose latent factors have finite support and may each feed multiple mechanisms; a realization lemma places every valid encoding inside the full ambient class. The exact checker enumerates the latent-support products, compares unnormalized selected atoms by cross multiplication, and compares postintervention selected targets by cross multiplication. The projection and certificate claims apply only to terminal Algorithm 1 calls rooted at \(D_i\in\mathcal D_S(D)\), with fixed single-S-component target \(C=D_i\) and a recursively shrunken single-S-component enclosure. novelty_justification: The proposal turns Abouei et al.'s sufficient latent S-ID algorithm into an exact graphwise criterion on their full childless-selector augmented-SCM class uniformly over every finite observed signature with at least two states per substantive variable, comparing models only within a fixed signature. Each actual terminal failure rooted at an Eq. 23 factor \(D_i\) is compiled into two exact rational finite-table certificates under the admissible binary signature. Their latent scopes allow genuine multi-mechanism sharing, an inclusion lemma realizes them inside the unrestricted published model class, and an exhaustive checker verifies normalized selected-law equality and target separation exactly. Unlike ordinary hedge completeness, the effective inverse construction must jointly realize virtual bidirected edges sharing or branching through selection ancestors while preserving every selected atom and an intervention-before-conditioning contrast. Chen et al. provide only a forward conditioning transformation, Kivva et al. use a multivalued positive perturbation rather than a binary S-Hedge lift, and Qiu et al. study distribution-class ATE recovery under unconfoundedness. The exact two-virtual-edge fiber separation is load-bearing, after which the effective arbitrary shared-ancestor lift is the genuine open content.
